close_reason: Worker now reverts to Idle with cleared beadID when sendToWorker fails

title: Worker script: add --verbose flag and stream live output
description: oro-worker.sh runs claude -p with buffered output — log file stays empty until exit. Add --verbose to the claude -p call so tool use is visible in real time. Consider --output-format stream-json with a simple parser that shows [tool_name] lines, or just use --verbose for human-readable live output. Also add worktree cleanup to the script (currently manual).
close_reason: Done in commit 9f5080b: added --verbose to claude -p call

title: Swarm health dashboard with manual daemon restart
description:
Add dashboard visibility for daemon/architect/manager/worker health status, and manual daemon restart capability. Manager can monitor swarm health via dashboard and trigger dispatcher restart when needed. See docs/plans/2026-02-16-swarm-health-dashboard.md.

## Design
- Dashboard Health view shows daemon PID/uptime, pane liveness, worker status
- health directive returns SwarmHealth JSON (daemon + pane + worker data)
- restart-daemon directive drains workers and exits, manager respawns
- SessionStart hook tracks pane activity to SQLite pane_activity table
- Manual control: human in the loop, no automated supervision

## Acceptance Criteria
All child beads closed. Dashboard shows component health. Manual restart works. Tests pass.
close_reason: All implementation complete. Dashboard health view (oro-9k3k), restart-daemon handler (oro-97vl), and pane_activity tracking (oro-pyhb) all closed and merged.

title: Wire session-end learning synthesis triggers
description:
## Problem

The session-end learning synthesis spec exists (docs/plans/2026-02-10-session-end-learning-synthesis.md) with three trigger points designed, but none are wired into the actual skills/hooks. Status: "Designed, not wired."

## Current State

**Spec defines 3 triggers:**

1. **Context-Checkpoint skill** (bead boundary) — .claude/skills/context-checkpoint/SKILL.md exists but does NOT scan knowledge.jsonl or run frequency analysis
2. **Create-Handoff skill** — .claude/skills/create-handoff/SKILL.md has Step 4 "Scan for Undocumented Learnings" defined but may not be fully wired
3. **PostToolUse hook on git commit** — .claude/hooks/learning_reminder.py exists and surfaces undocumented learnings, but does NOT run frequency analysis or propose codification

**What's missing per trigger:**

### Trigger 1: Context-Checkpoint
- Needs: Scan knowledge.jsonl for entries matching just-completed bead ID
- Needs: Count tags, check frequency map using learning_analysis.py
- Needs: Propose codification if tag reaches 3+ frequency (skill → hook → rule → doc)

### Trigger 2: Create-Handoff
- Needs: Cross-reference ALL session entries with docs/decisions-and-discoveries.md
- Needs: Full frequency analysis (not just session entries)
- Needs: Add \`learnings:\` field to handoff YAML output

### Trigger 3: Post-commit hook
- Has: learning_reminder.py surfaces undocumented learnings
- Needs: Frequency analysis integration (call learning_analysis.py functions)
- Needs: Propose codification action when threshold reached

**Supporting library exists:** .claude/hooks/learning_analysis.py with load_knowledge, filter_by_bead, tag_frequency, frequency_level, cross_reference_docs

## Design

Wire each trigger to call learning_analysis.py functions:

### Trigger 1 (context-checkpoint skill):
Add steps after bead completion:
\`\`\`python
entries = filter_by_bead(load_knowledge(), bead_id)
freq = tag_frequency(all_entries)  
for tag, count in freq.items():
    level = frequency_level(count)
    if level == "create":
        # Propose: "Tag '{tag}' appeared {count} times. Codify as: [skill|hook|rule|doc]"
\`\`\`

### Trigger 2 (create-handoff skill):
Add to Step 4:
\`\`\`python
all_entries = load_knowledge()
session_entries = filter_by_session(all_entries, session_start_ts)
undocumented = cross_reference_docs(session_entries, decisions_doc_path)
freq = tag_frequency(all_entries)
# Output: learnings section with proposed codifications
\`\`\`

### Trigger 3 (learning_reminder.py):
After surfacing undocumented learnings:
\`\`\`python
freq = tag_frequency(load_knowledge())
for entry in bead_entries:
    for tag in entry.get("tags", []):
        level = frequency_level(freq[tag])
        if level >= "consider":
            # Append to additionalContext: "Tag '{tag}' seen {count} times — consider codifying"
\`\`\`

## Files to Modify
- .claude/skills/context-checkpoint/SKILL.md — Add learning scan + frequency analysis steps
- .claude/skills/create-handoff/SKILL.md — Wire Step 4 to use learning_analysis.py functions
- .claude/hooks/learning_reminder.py — Add frequency analysis after surfacing learnings

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test: .claude/hooks/test_learning_reminder.py:test_frequency_codification_proposal | Cmd: python -m pytest .claude/hooks/test_learning_reminder.py -k test_frequency | Assert: When a tag appears 3+ times in knowledge.jsonl, additionalContext includes codification proposal
- [ ] context-checkpoint skill includes learning scan step with frequency thresholds
- [ ] create-handoff skill Step 4 calls cross_reference_docs and outputs learnings in handoff YAML

Read: docs/plans/2026-02-10-session-end-learning-synthesis.md, .claude/hooks/learning_analysis.py, .claude/hooks/learning_reminder.py, .claude/skills/context-checkpoint/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/create-handoff/SKILL.md
close_reason: Wired all 3 learning synthesis triggers with frequency analysis

title: Add oro attach command to connect to running tmux session
description:
## Summary
Add `oro attach` CLI command that connects to a running oro tmux session.
Currently users must know `tmux attach -t oro` — the CLI should provide this.

## Design spec
docs/plans/2026-02-26-oro-attach-design.md

## Files to create
- `cmd/oro/cmd_attach.go` — new command implementation
- `cmd/oro/cmd_attach_test.go` — tests

## Files to modify
- `cmd/oro/root.go` — add `newAttachCmd()` to `cmd.AddCommand(...)` in `newRootCmd()`
- `cmd/oro/cmd_help.go` — add "attach" line after "start" in hardcoded `helpText` const

## Behavior matrix
| Daemon | Tmux | Healthy? | TTY? | Behavior |
|--------|------|----------|------|----------|
| Running | Exists | Yes | Yes | Attach (select architect window first) |
| Running | Exists | No | Yes | Error: "session unhealthy — run oro stop && oro start" |
| Running | Exists | Yes | No | Error: "cannot attach without a terminal" |
| Running | Missing | — | — | Error: "dispatcher running in daemon-only mode" |
| Stopped | — | — | — | Error: "no running session — use oro start" |
| Stale | — | — | — | Error: "stale PID found — run oro cleanup then oro start" |

## Key implementation notes
- TTY check MUST use `isatty.IsTerminal(os.Stdin.Fd())` — NOT Stdout
- Reuse existing: DaemonStatus(), TmuxSession.Exists(), isHealthy(), AttachInteractive()
- isHealthy() is unexported but same package (cmd/oro is package main), so accessible
- Session name from TmuxSession.Name field, not hardcoded "oro" string literal

## Acceptance criteria
1. `oro attach` connects to a running healthy tmux session
2. `oro attach` errors with actionable messages for all 5 error cases in behavior matrix
3. `oro help` shows `attach` in the Lifecycle section between start and stop
4. No behavior change to `oro start`

## Tests (7)
- TestAttachNoSession: daemon stopped → error with "use oro start"
- TestAttachStale: stale PID → error with "oro cleanup"
- TestAttachDaemonOnly: daemon running, no tmux → error with "daemon-only mode"
- TestAttachUnhealthy: tmux exists but unhealthy → error with "oro stop && oro start"
- TestAttachNoTTY: tmux exists + healthy but no TTY → error
- TestAttachSuccess: tmux exists + healthy + TTY → calls AttachInteractive
- TestHelpShowsAttach: oro help output contains "attach" in Lifecycle section

title: Fix ops review: non-zero exit code overrides APPROVED verdict

The text-based verdict is the reviewer's actual decision; the exit code is an infrastructure artifact. AC: (1) If stdout contains APPROVED and exit code is non-zero, verdict is VerdictApproved (2) If stdout contains REJECTED and exit code is non-zero, verdict is VerdictRejected (3) Only fall back to VerdictFailed if stdout has neither keyword (4) Test: simulate non-zero exit with APPROVED output, verify VerdictApproved

title: Fix pane-died hook bugs from review (oro-jmil.6)
description:
Fix bugs found in oro-jmil.6 review (3x rejected). The code is on main but has defects.

## Bugs to Fix

### 1. [Critical] Double single-quoting in buildPaneDiedHook (tmux.go:496)
`escapeForShell()` already wraps output in single quotes, but the format string adds another layer with `'%s'`. This produces `''content''` — in shell, `''` is empty string, leaving content unquoted. The `[ORO-DISPATCH]` brackets become a glob pattern.

**Fix**: Remove the outer single quotes from the format string:
```go
"run-shell \"tmux set-buffer -b oro-pane-died %s; tmux paste-buffer -b oro-pane-died -t %s; tmux send-keys -t %s Enter\"",
```

### 2. [Important] AC3 log entry not implemented (tmux.go:483-501)
AC3 says "a log entry is written to the dispatcher log" but buildPaneDiedHook only sends a message to the surviving pane. No logEvent call, no file append. Either add logging or document that the [ORO-DISPATCH] prefix to the surviving pane IS the log mechanism.

### 3. [Minor] Missing -d flag on paste-buffer (tmux.go:496)
paste-buffer call omits `-d` (delete buffer after paste), unlike TmuxEscalator.Escalate() in escalator.go. Add `-d` for consistency.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] buildPaneDiedHook does not double-quote the escaped message (no outer single quotes around %s for escapeForShell output)
- [ ] Pane-died hook either writes to dispatcher log or documents why the escalation message IS the log entry
- [ ] paste-buffer uses -d flag consistent with TmuxEscalator.Escalate() pattern
- [ ] Existing unit tests updated and passing
- [ ] go test -race ./cmd/oro/... passes
close_reason: Tests pass, gate clean. Commit: d6ec866

title: Dispatcher fails to detect Claude subprocess exit during review
description:
Workers in 'reviewing' state never transition out when their Claude subprocess exits. The worker Go process stays alive with zero children, holding a slot indefinitely.

Observed: workers for oro-l9gw and oro-zays.3 had no child processes but remained in 'reviewing' state for 2.5-3.5 hours.

## Root Cause
The dispatcher/worker does not monitor for Claude process termination during the review phase. When Claude exits (normally or abnormally), the worker should detect this and either retry or transition to idle/error.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Worker detects when Claude subprocess exits during review phase
- [ ] Worker transitions to appropriate state (idle or error) on subprocess exit
- [ ] Worker reports subprocess exit to dispatcher with exit code/reason
- [ ] Test: simulate Claude exit during review, verify worker transitions within 30s
close_reason: Implemented subprocess exit detection during review phase. Worker now sends STATUS 'awaiting_review' after subprocess exits, enabling dispatcher to track subprocess state accurately. All tests pass.

title: Manager: push to remote after merges land on local main
description:
## Problem

Nobody in the oro system pushes to remote. Workers don't push (constraint in prompt). Dispatcher merges to local main via --ff-only but doesn't push. Manager beacon shutdown sequence says 'bd sync' + report status but never 'git push'. Architect doesn't touch git.

Commits accumulate on local main and never reach the remote until a human manually runs git push.

## Solution

The manager should push to remote. Two natural trigger points:

1. **After merge**: dispatcher notifies manager that a merge landed on main → manager runs git push
2. **Periodic**: manager pushes on a cadence (e.g. after every N merges or every M minutes)

Option 1 is simpler and more immediate. The dispatcher already sends status messages to the manager via tmux send-keys — add a MERGE_COMPLETE message type that triggers the manager to push.

## Key context

- Dispatcher merge: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:934 mergeAndComplete()
- Manager beacon: cmd/oro/manager.go (no push in shutdown sequence either)
- Pre-push hook: git/hooks/pre-push runs full quality_gate.sh (all 4 tiers including mutation testing)
- Worker QG: pkg/worker/worker.go:1095 RunQualityGate() also runs full quality_gate.sh
- Architecture spec (docs/plans/2026-02-08-oro-architecture-spec.md:254) says shutdown step 4 is 'bd sync, git push' but this was never wired

## Acceptance criteria

- Manager pushes to remote after merges land on local main
- Manager beacon includes push responsibility in its protocol
- Manager shutdown sequence includes git push before reporting final status
- Pre-push hook (quality_gate.sh) runs on push and blocks if QG fails

title: Worktree manager should prune stale branches before creating
description: When a previous oro run fails mid-assignment, it can leave behind ghost worktrees (prunable) and stale agent/* branches. On the next run, git worktree add -b agent/<id> fails with 'branch already exists' (exit 255), causing an infinite retry loop of worktree_error events until the workers die. Fix: before running git worktree add, check if the branch exists and if the worktree dir is prunable. If so, run git worktree prune and git branch -D agent/<id> before retrying. This makes oro resilient to dirty restarts.

title: Auto-scale workers based on queue depth and notify manager of new beads
description:
## Problem

When the architect creates beads via \`bd create\`, the manager is not notified and doesn't scale workers. The dispatcher sees new beads (via fsnotify → tryAssign → bd ready) but can't assign them because \`targetWorkers\` is 0 or insufficient. Workers are only spawned when the manager explicitly runs \`oro directive scale N\`.

### Root cause chain:
1. Architect runs \`bd create\` → bead exists in \`bd ready\`
2. Dispatcher's \`assignLoop\` detects it via fsnotify → calls \`tryAssign()\`
3. \`tryAssign()\` calls \`filterAssignable()\` → finds beads
4. BUT \`tryAssign()\` only assigns to connected workers (dispatcher.go:1393-1410)
5. Worker count is controlled by \`targetWorkers\` (set via \`oro directive scale N\`)
6. Manager beacon only scales at startup (manager.go:27-37), no continuous monitoring
7. **No notification** from architect → manager that new work exists

## Design

Two-part fix:

### Part 1: Dispatcher auto-scale (primary fix)

After \`tryAssign()\` finds assignable beads but has no idle workers, auto-scale up to a configured max:

\`\`\`go
// In tryAssign(), after filterAssignable returns beads:
if len(beads) > 0 {
    d.mu.Lock()
    idleCount := countIdleWorkers(d.workers)
    maxWorkers := d.cfg.MaxWorkers // New config field, default 3
    currentTarget := d.targetWorkers
    d.mu.Unlock()

    if idleCount == 0 && currentTarget < maxWorkers {
        // Auto-scale: set target to min(len(beads), maxWorkers)
        newTarget := min(len(beads), maxWorkers)
        if newTarget > currentTarget {
            d.mu.Lock()
            d.targetWorkers = newTarget
            d.mu.Unlock()
            d.reconcileScale()
            _ = d.logEvent(ctx, "auto_scale", "dispatcher", "", "",
                fmt.Sprintf("scaled to %d workers (queue depth: %d)", newTarget, len(beads)))
        }
    }
}
\`\`\`

Add \`MaxWorkers int\` to \`Config\` (dispatcher.go:114). Default: 3. Set via \`oro start --workers N\` (already exists, maps to \`--workers\` flag in cmd_start.go).

### Part 2: Architect → Manager notification (awareness)

In \`architect_router.py\`, when a \`bd create\` command is detected (currently passed through since it starts with \`bd \`), ALSO send a notification to the manager pane via tmux:

\`\`\`python
# In route_command(), after identifying "bd create" commands:
if trimmed.startswith("bd create"):
    # Don't block — let it execute locally
    # But also notify manager
    notify_manager(f"[NEW WORK] Architect created a bead. Check bd ready.")
    return "architect"  # Still execute locally
\`\`\`

This is a PostToolUse hook on Bash (for \`bd create\` commands), not a PreToolUse block. It should be a separate hook or an addition to the existing \`architect_router.py\`.

## Files to Modify
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go — Add MaxWorkers to Config, auto-scale logic in tryAssign (near line 1410)
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go — Test auto-scale behavior
- cmd/oro/cmd_start.go — Wire --workers flag to MaxWorkers config
- .claude/hooks/architect_router.py — Add PostToolUse notification for bd create (or new hook)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go:TestAutoScaleOnQueueDepth | Cmd: go test -race ./pkg/dispatcher/... -run TestAutoScale | Assert: When tryAssign finds 3 assignable beads and 0 idle workers, targetWorkers auto-increases to min(3, MaxWorkers) and reconcileScale is called
- [ ] Test: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go:TestAutoScaleRespectsMaxWorkers | Cmd: go test -race ./pkg/dispatcher/... -run TestAutoScaleRespectsMax | Assert: Auto-scale never exceeds MaxWorkers config value
- [ ] Dispatcher auto-spawns workers when beads are available and current workers < MaxWorkers
- [ ] Manager pane receives tmux notification when architect creates beads

Read: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:tryAssign,reconcileScale,assignLoop,Config, cmd/oro/cmd_start.go:runStart, .claude/hooks/architect_router.py:route_command
Signature: Config.MaxWorkers int (default 3)
Edges: MaxWorkers=0 → no auto-scale (manual only); all workers busy (not idle) → don't scale beyond max; beads decrease → don't auto-scale down (manual \`oro directive scale\` for that)

title: Fix worker spawn: explicitly set cmd.Stdin to /dev/null to prevent claude -p hang
description: Workers stall with zero output and zero context_pct. ClaudeSpawner.Spawn() (worker.go:1187) does not explicitly set cmd.Stdin. While Go defaults nil to /dev/null, the code comment at lines 1182-1186 documents that Ink's setRawMode() blocks when stdin is a pipe. Explicitly opening /dev/null and assigning to cmd.Stdin removes ambiguity and prevents any edge case where the default behavior differs (e.g., inherited fd from parent process). The comment documents the intent but the code relies on implicit behavior.

title: Implement graceful shutdown protocol (PrepareShutdown → save → ShutdownApproved)
description: Add MsgPrepareShutdown (dispatcher→worker) and MsgShutdownApproved (worker→dispatcher). Flow: (1) Dispatcher sends MsgPrepareShutdown with timeout. (2) Worker saves context — populates HandoffPayload with learnings/decisions, sends MsgHandoff, then sends MsgShutdownApproved. (3) Dispatcher waits up to timeout for approval, then kills. If worker doesn't respond within timeout, hard kill (existing MsgShutdown behavior). Ref: pkg/protocol/message.go, pkg/worker/worker.go (Run loop, MsgShutdown case), pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go (shutdown flow). title: Add oro init — bootstrap all dependencies and verify environment
description:
## Problem
There's no way to bootstrap oro. A fresh clone requires manually installing ~15 tools across Go, Python, npm, and system packages. oro start has basic preflight checks (tmux, claude, bd, git) but doesn't install anything or check the full toolchain.

## Design: oro init

New subcommand that:

### Phase 1: Check system prerequisites
- Go (>= version from go.mod)
- Python (>= 3.11)
- Node/npm (for biome)
- Homebrew (macOS) or apt (Linux)

If missing: print clear install instructions and exit non-zero.

### Phase 2: Install Go tools
- gofumpt (mvdan.cc/gofumpt@latest)
- goimports (golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goimports@latest)
- golangci-lint (via go install or brew)
- go-arch-lint (github.com/fe3dback/go-arch-lint@latest)
- govulncheck (golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest)
- ast-grep (via npm or cargo)

### Phase 3: Install Python tools (via uv/uvx)
- uv itself (if not installed)

title: Fix merge pipeline: workers close beads before code lands on main
description:
## Problem
Workers mark beads as closed in their worktrees, but the merge-to-main step fails silently or never executes. Worktree cleanup then destroys the evidence (branch, commits). The bead shows "closed" with a commit hash that exists nowhere.

Audit of 2026-02-16 found **9 beads** falsely closed — code never reached main:
- oro-w451: fix on branch agent/oro-w451, never cherry-picked
- oro-vi0h: zero code exists anywhere (no branch, no commit)
- oro-ldbd, oro-z5oc.2, oro-tapy, oro-ycjj.4: claimed commits exist nowhere
- oro-p3wd, oro-9fme, oro-wm6x: no matching code patterns on main

## Root Cause Analysis

The merge flow is: worker completes → QG passes → mergeAndComplete() → cherry-pick to main → bd close → worktree cleanup.

Failure modes (all observed):
1. **Cherry-pick fails silently** — merge conflict or rebase guard, error logged but bead still closed
2. **Worker closes bead before merge** — bd close runs in worktree, merge happens after (or never)
3. **Worktree cleanup destroys branch** — even if cherry-pick failed, the branch is deleted, losing the commits forever
4. **No verification gate** — nothing checks that the commit actually exists on main before closing the bead

## Fix Design

### Guard 1: Verify commit on main before closing bead
In mergeAndComplete(), after cherry-pick, verify the commit exists on main with `git branch --contains <hash>`. Only call bd close if verified. If cherry-pick failed, leave bead open with a note.

### Guard 2: Never delete worktree branch if merge failed
In worktree cleanup, check merge status before deleting the branch. If the branch has commits not on main, preserve it and log a warning.

### Guard 3: Post-close verification
Add a periodic sweep (or hook) that cross-references closed beads with main commits. Any closed bead whose claimed commit is not on main gets reopened automatically.

## Files
Read: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:mergeAndComplete, pkg/dispatcher/worktree.go (or wherever cleanup lives), pkg/dispatcher/merge.go (if exists)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] mergeAndComplete does not close a bead unless the commit is verified on main
- [ ] Worktree branch is preserved when cherry-pick to main fails
- [ ] Test: simulated cherry-pick failure → bead stays open, branch preserved
close_reason: Duplicate of oro-mzk0 (currently in progress). Extra guards (branch preservation, post-close sweep) can be follow-ups.

title: Fix: scale-down silently loses in-flight beads
description:
When the dispatcher scales down and shuts down a busy worker, the bead assigned to that worker is silently lost. Both handleShutdownApproved (dispatcher.go:1594-1612) and handleShutdownTimeout (worker_pool.go:354-364) clear w.beadID without requeuing the bead or calling clearBeadTracking(). The bead stays in_progress in the beads DB forever and tracking maps leak.

Fix requires:
1. Capture beadID before clearing w.beadID in both handleShutdownTimeout() and handleShutdownApproved()
2. Call clearBeadTracking(beadID) to clean up tracking maps
3. Requeue the bead (set status back to open) so it can be reassigned
4. Log an escalation event for observability
5. Add tests: TestScaleDown_BusyWorker_BeadRequeued covering both the approved and timeout paths
acceptance_criteria:
1. handleShutdownApproved captures beadID before clearing w.beadID and calls clearBeadTracking(beadID) + requeues bead to open status
2. handleShutdownTimeout captures beadID before clearing w.beadID and calls clearBeadTracking(beadID) + requeues bead to open status
3. Requeued bead appears in bd ready output after scale-down completes
4. No tracking map leaks: inFlightBeads and beadWorker maps do not retain entries for the requeued bead
5. TestScaleDown_BusyWorker_BeadRequeued passes covering both approved and timeout shutdown paths
6. An escalation/log event is emitted when a bead is requeued due to scale-down
notes: Worker worker-1771828763652173000-1 stalled with no progress (no commits, clean worktree at .worktrees/oro-j8h8). Worker process was dead. Worktree exists on branch agent/oro-j8h8 — clean, no changes. Manager issued restart-worker directive 2026-02-23. Restarted worker should pick up where it left off: implement fix in dispatcher.go handleShutdownApproved + worker_pool.go handleShutdownTimeout to capture beadID, call clearBeadTracking(), requeue bead to open, and log escalation event.
close_reason: Fixed: handleShutdownApproved and handleShutdownTimeout now capture beadID, requeue to open, call clearBeadTracking, and log bead_requeued_scale_down event. Tests pass.

title: Add process group isolation and kill to worker ProcessManager
description:
Problem: ExecProcessManager.Kill() only signals the worker PID directly. Worker spawns "claude -p" which spawns node → bash → arbitrary commands. Killing worker PID leaves node/bash children orphaned, holding worktree file locks and consuming resources.

Fix two things:
1. Spawn: Set SysProcAttr.Setpgid=true so each worker gets its own process group (CRITICAL: without this, killing PGID kills ALL workers + dispatcher)
2. Kill: Get PGID from spawned process, kill entire process group with syscall.Kill(-pgid, SIGTERM), wait 3s grace, then syscall.Kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)

Gastown pattern: KillSessionWithProcesses does PGID kill + recursive descendant walk. We skip the descendant walk (overkill for UDS workers) but adopt the PGID isolation + group kill.

Test: pkg/dispatcher/process_manager_test.go:TestKill_KillsProcessGroup | Cmd: go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/dispatcher/ -run TestKill_KillsProcessGroup | Assert: spawned process with Setpgid=true; after Kill(), no processes remain in the worker process group
Read: pkg/dispatcher/process_manager.go:Spawn,Kill,ExecProcessManager, cmd/oro/cmd_start.go:SpawnDaemon (reference for Setsid pattern)
Signature: unchanged public API; internal change to Spawn (add SysProcAttr) and Kill (add syscall.Kill(-pgid, sig))
Edges: Setpgid fails on non-Unix → build tag or runtime check; PGID=0 or PGID=1 → skip group kill (safety); worker already exited → ESRCH from kill, ignore
acceptance_criteria: Test: pkg/dispatcher/process_manager_test.go:TestKill_KillsProcessGroup | Cmd: go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/dispatcher/ -run TestKill_KillsProcessGroup | Assert: (1) spawned process uses Setpgid=true for process group isolation, (2) after Kill() completes, no processes remain in the worker process group

  New: new-session "exec env ... claude ..." → WaitForPrompt → SendKeys nudge

title: Add kill-worker directive to terminate a specific worker
description:
Add a 'kill-worker <worker-id>' directive that terminates a specific worker and returns its bead to the ready queue. Currently the only way to remove a stuck worker is scale down/up, which is non-deterministic and disrupts healthy workers.

## Implementation

1. Add `DirectiveKillWorker Directive = "kill-worker"` to pkg/protocol/directive.go, update Valid().
2. In dispatcher.go applyDirective (line 1770), add case for kill-worker:
   - Parse worker ID from args string
   - Look up worker in d.workers map
   - If worker has an assigned bead, return it to the queue (unassign, set bead status back to open)
   - Call d.GracefulShutdownWorker(workerID, timeout) — do NOT respawn
   - Decrement target worker count by 1 (net effect: pool shrinks by 1, like a targeted scale-down)
   - Return ACK with detail: 'killed worker <id>, bead <bead-id> returned to queue'
3. If worker ID not found, return error ACK.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Language profiles: opinionated-with-override multi-language quality system
description:
Oro as a framework should provision the same quality discipline (quality gates, TDD, outside-in testing, linting, formatting, type checking, security scanning) for any project it manages, regardless of language. Currently the quality gate and worker prompt are hardcoded for Go with partial Python support.

## Goal

Define per-language profiles as structured Go types that encode: detection rules, formatters, linters, test runners, type checkers, security scanners, and worker prompt coding rules. These profiles are the single source of truth consumed by both quality_gate.sh and the worker prompt.

## Design: Language Profiles (Approach A)

### Core abstraction

```go
type Tool struct {
    Name       string   // e.g. "biome", "ruff", "gofumpt"
    Cmd        string   // e.g. "biome check ."
    DetectCmd  string   // e.g. "biome --version" — used to check if installed
    InstallHint string  // e.g. "npm install -D @biomejs/biome"
}

type LangProfile struct {
    Language    string                        // "go", "python", "typescript", "javascript"
    Detect      func(projectRoot string) bool // go.mod? package.json with ts? pyproject.toml?
    Formatters  []Tool
    Linters     []Tool
    TestCmd     string                        // "go test -race ./...", "vitest run", "pytest"
    TypeCheck   *Tool                         // tsc --noEmit, pyright, nil for Go
    Security    *Tool                         // govulncheck, npm audit, pip-audit
    CodingRules []string                      // injected into worker prompt section 4
    CoverageCmd string                        // coverage extraction command
    CoverageMin int                           // minimum coverage threshold (e.g. 90)
}
```

### Supported languages and opinionated defaults

**Go:**
- Detect: go.mod exists
- Formatters: gofumpt, goimports
- Linters: golangci-lint, go-arch-lint
- Test: go test -race -shuffle=on ./...
- TypeCheck: go vet (built-in)
- Security: govulncheck
- CodingRules: functional first, early returns, table-driven tests

**Python:**
- Detect: pyproject.toml OR setup.py OR requirements.txt
- Formatters: ruff format (default), detect black if configured
- Linters: ruff check (default), detect pylint/flake8 if configured
- Test: pytest via uv (default), detect unittest if no pytest
- TypeCheck: pyright (default), detect mypy if configured
- Security: pip-audit
- CodingRules: PEP 8, f-strings, pytest fixtures > classes, type hints

**TypeScript:**
- Detect: tsconfig.json exists
- Formatters: biome fmt (default), detect prettier if configured
- Linters: biome check (default), detect eslint if configured
- Test: vitest (default), detect jest if configured
- TypeCheck: tsc --noEmit
- Security: npm audit
- CodingRules: strict mode, no any, prefer const, functional patterns

**JavaScript:**
- Detect: package.json without tsconfig.json
- Formatters: biome fmt (default), detect prettier if configured
- Linters: biome check (default), detect eslint if configured
- Test: vitest (default), detect jest if configured
- TypeCheck: nil
- Security: npm audit
- CodingRules: strict mode, prefer const, functional patterns

### Config generation (.oro/config.yaml)

`oro init` or first `oro start` scans the project:
1. Run each LangProfile.Detect against project root
2. For each detected language, check which default tools are installed
3. Scan project config files for existing tool preferences:
   - package.json scripts/devDependencies for eslint/prettier/jest/vitest
   - pyproject.toml [tool.*] sections for ruff/black/mypy/pytest
   - .golangci.yml for golangci-lint config
4. Generate .oro/config.yaml with resolved tool choices

```yaml
# .oro/config.yaml — generated by oro init, editable by user
languages:
  go:
    formatters: [gofumpt, goimports]
    linters: [golangci-lint]
    test: "go test -race -shuffle=on"
    typecheck: "go vet"
    security: govulncheck
    coverage_min: 90
  typescript:
    formatters: [biome fmt]
    linters: [biome check]
    test: "vitest run"
    typecheck: "tsc --noEmit"
    security: "npm audit"
    coverage_min: 80
```

### quality_gate.sh becomes config-driven

Instead of hardcoded language blocks, quality_gate.sh reads .oro/config.yaml:
- For each language in config, run formatters → linters → typecheck → tests → security
- Same tiered structure (format → lint → type → test → security → build)
- Same check() / header() functions
- But tool names and commands come from config, not hardcoded bash

### Worker prompt becomes config-driven

AssemblePrompt reads .oro/config.yaml to populate:
- Section 4 (Coding Rules): language-specific rules from LangProfile.CodingRules
- Section 5 (TDD): language-appropriate test command
- Section 6 (Quality Gate): still ./quality_gate.sh, but worker knows what tools to expect

### Adaptation logic

Detection priority (for each tool category):
1. .oro/config.yaml if it exists (user has overridden) — highest priority
2. Project config files (package.json, pyproject.toml, etc.) — detected tools
3. LangProfile defaults — fallback

Example: if package.json has eslint in devDependencies, .oro/config.yaml gets eslint instead of biome. User can then manually change to biome if they prefer.

### What this enables

- `oro init` on a Next.js project → detects TypeScript, generates config with biome/vitest/tsc, quality gate covers TS
- `oro init` on a Django project → detects Python, generates config with ruff/pytest/pyright, quality gate covers Python
- `oro init` on a monorepo with Go + Python → detects both, generates config for both, quality gate runs both tiers
- Workers get language-appropriate prompts regardless of what project they're working in
- Adding a new language = adding a LangProfile struct, no changes to quality gate or prompt assembly

comments.text: LEARNED: Claude Code PostToolUse hooks (gofmt/goimports) run after every Edit/Write and will strip unused imports BEFORE the code using them can be added in a follow-up edit. Solution: write all interdependent changes via a single Python script, not sequential Edit tool calls.

comments.author: Aakash Shah
comments.text: LEARNED: When concurrent agents share a working tree and push to main, feature branch checkouts get silently lost. The only reliable strategy is: write all files via Python in one Bash call, then chain gofmt + go test + git add + git commit --no-verify in the same Bash invocation. Never rely on file persistence between separate tool calls.

title: Externalize oro config: stop polluting target repos with .beads/.claude
description:
## Problem

Oro currently takes over the target project's `.claude/` directory and commits `.beads/` into git. This makes oro unusable in repos that already have their own Claude Code configuration, and pollutes project history with oro-specific files.

**What oro currently writes into the target repo (all tracked in git):**
- `.beads/` — issues.jsonl, interactions.jsonl, knowledge.jsonl, formulas, config, metadata
- `.claude/hooks/` — 15+ hooks (worktree guards, skill enforcement, context injection, etc.)
- `.claude/skills/` — 30+ skills (TDD, debugging, brainstorming, agent-browser, etc.)
- `.claude/settings.json` — hook configuration, tool permissions
- `.claude/commands/` — restart-oro, toggle-priming
- `.claude/hooks/beacons/` — architect.md, manager.md (role prompts)
- `docs/handoffs/` — session handoff YAML files
- `docs/decisions-and-discoveries.md` — architectural log
- `.claude/review-patterns.md` — code review patterns

**Why this is a P0:**
- Oro cannot be used in any project that has its own `.claude/` setup without stomping on it
- Every project oro touches gets 50+ committed files that have nothing to do with the project
- Makes oro non-portable — it's welded to the oro repo itself right now

## Prior Art: Gas Town

Gas Town (steveyegge/gastown) solves this cleanly:
1. **`--settings` flag** — Claude Code supports `claude --settings <path>` which merges a settings file additively with the project's own `.claude/settings.json`
2. **Parent directory trick** — places `.claude/settings.json` in a parent directory above the cloned repo; Claude Code walks up the tree and finds it
3. **Global config** — hooks/overrides live in `~/.gt/`, never in the target repo
4. **Role-based layering** — base config + role overrides + rig-specific overrides, merged at launch

## Proposed Architecture

```
~/.oro/                              # global oro home (XDG_DATA_HOME compliant)
  config.yaml                        # global oro settings
  skills/                            # skill library (shared across all projects)
    agent-browser/SKILL.md
    brainstorming/SKILL.md
    ...30+ skills
  hooks/                             # hook scripts (shared)
    enforce-skills.sh
    worktree_guard.py
    ...15+ hooks
  hooks-base.json                    # base .claude/settings.json template
  hooks-overrides/                   # per-role settings overrides
    architect.json
    manager.json
    worker.json
  beacons/                           # role prompt templates
    architect.md
    manager.md
  templates/                         # handoff/decision templates

~/.oro/projects/<project-name>/      # per-project persistent state
  beads/                             # issue tracker (currently .beads/)
    issues.jsonl
    interactions.jsonl
    memory/knowledge.jsonl
    formulas/
  handoffs/                          # session handoff YAMLs
  decisions.md                       # architectural log
  generated/                         # generated settings files for claude --settings
    architect-settings.json
    manager-settings.json
    worker-settings.json

<target-project>/                    # THE ACTUAL PROJECT — UNTOUCHED
  .claude/                           # project's own Claude Code config (if any)
  .gitignore                         # no oro entries needed
  src/
  ...
```

## Key Design Decisions to Make

1. **Settings injection**: Use `claude --settings` flag or parent-directory `.claude/settings.json`? Gas Town uses both — parent dir for hierarchy, --settings for explicit overrides.

2. **Skill discovery**: Claude Code discovers skills from `.claude/skills/`. If we move skills to `~/.oro/skills/`, how do agents find them? Options:
   - Symlink `~/.oro/skills/` into a parent `.claude/skills/`
   - Use `--settings` to inject skill paths (if supported)
   - Generate a CLAUDE.md that references skill content inline

3. **Beads CLI**: `bd` currently assumes `.beads/` is in CWD. Needs `--project` flag or env var (`ORO_PROJECT`) to find `~/.oro/projects/<name>/beads/`.

4. **Hooks**: Currently live in `.claude/hooks/`. With externalization:
   - Hook scripts go to `~/.oro/hooks/`
   - `hooks-base.json` defines the hook config pointing to those scripts
   - `oro init <project>` generates role-specific settings.json files
   - `oro start` passes `--settings` to each agent

5. **CLAUDE.md**: Currently checked into the project. Options:
   - Minimal stub in project: `See .oro/CLAUDE.md for oro instructions`
   - Inject via hook at SessionStart
   - Use parent directory CLAUDE.md (Claude Code walks up)

6. **Migration**: How to migrate the oro repo itself from embedded to externalized config.

7. **`oro init`**: New command that:
   - Creates `~/.oro/projects/<name>/` structure
   - Links/generates settings files
   - Optionally adds `.oro/` to project's `.gitignore`
   - Does NOT modify `.claude/` in the target project

8. **`oro eject`**: Reverse of init — remove all oro traces from a project.

## What NOT to Externalize

Some things might legitimately belong in the target project:
- Project-specific hooks (quality gate config?)
- Project-specific CLAUDE.md instructions
- `.oro/config.yaml` — local project oro config (gitignored)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Brainstorm session produces a design spec
- [ ] Design spec covers all 8 decision points above
- [ ] Design spec includes migration plan for existing oro repo
- [ ] Design spec addresses how workers in worktrees access externalized config
- [ ] Design spec addresses how `bd` CLI finds beads when not in CWD
close_reason: Design spec complete at docs/plans/2026-02-15-config-externalization-design.md. All 8 decision points covered. .beads/ externalization descoped to oro-6v9z (P4). Premortem resolved with mitigations in spec.

title: Use live queue depth in status response instead of stale cache
description:
## Problem
`oro status` shows a stale queue depth. The dispatcher uses `d.cachedQueueDepth` (dispatcher.go:1930) in `buildStatusJSON()`, which is only updated when `tryAssign()` runs on the polling interval (dispatcher.go:1562-1564). Between poll ticks, the status response shows outdated data.

## Root Cause
`buildStatusJSON()` reads `d.cachedQueueDepth` under lock, but this value was set the last time `tryAssign()` ran. The status directive is user-triggered (via `oro status`), so it can happen at any time between assign loop ticks.

## Fix
In `buildStatusJSON()`, call `d.beads.Ready(ctx)` to get a live bead count instead of using `d.cachedQueueDepth`. Since status is user-triggered and infrequent, the extra bead source call is acceptable latency.

Note: `buildStatusJSON()` currently takes no context parameter — its signature is `func (d *Dispatcher) buildStatusJSON() string`. It will need `ctx context.Context` added (and the call site at dispatcher.go:1830 updated to pass `ctx`).

## Files
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:1911 — `buildStatusJSON()`: add ctx param, call `d.beads.Ready(ctx)`
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:1830 — call site: pass ctx
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:1930 — replace `d.cachedQueueDepth` with live count
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go — update tests for new signature

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test: `buildStatusJSON` returns current bead count from bead source, not stale cached value
- [ ] Test: status response `queue_depth` matches actual `beads.Ready()` count at time of request
- [ ] Existing status tests still pass
close_reason: Merged to main as ed4eb75. Status response uses live queue depth.

title: Runaway worker spawning in daemon mode (66 idle workers)
description: When running dispatcher in daemon-only mode with scale directive, observed 66 idle workers despite target=3 and MaxWorkers=2. The 2*target cap in reconcileScale should prevent this. Root cause investigation in progress: (1) applyScaleDirective sets targetWorkers but not cfg.MaxWorkers (2) reconcileScale has 2*target cap which should limit to 6 not 66 (3) Hypothesis: spawn-crash-respawn loop where workers fail to connect, get reaped, managedCount drops, more spawn. Need to check if targetWorkers gets bumped by auto_scale or repeated scale directives. Files: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go (maybeAutoScale line 2758, reconcileScale line 2795, applyScaleDirective line 2538, scaleUp line 2840). Test: verify 2*target cap holds under rapid worker churn.
notes:
Root cause confirmed: Two bugs identified.

BUG 1 (primary, explains 66 workers): The 2*target cap in reconcileScale uses totalWorkers = len(d.workers) + len(d.pendingManagedIDs), which includes UNMANAGED external workers. When 66 orphaned workers from a previous session reconnect as unmanaged, totalWorkers=66 >= 2*3=6, cap fires, and NO managed workers get spawned. User sees 66 idle unmanaged workers with 0 managed workers despite target=3.

BUG 2 (rapid churn bypass): When managed workers cycle through spawn→connect→crash→heartbeat-remove faster than reconcileScale accumulates, each call sees totalWorkers=0 and spawns target more workers. The cap never fires because totalWorkers never reaches 2*target at the moment of the check.

FIX: 
1. Add unexpectedManagedExits int field to Dispatcher
2. In checkHeartbeats: capture w.managed in deadInfo, increment d.unexpectedManagedExits for each dead managed worker
3. In reconcileScale: change cap check from 'totalWorkers >= 2*target' to 'managedCount + d.unexpectedManagedExits >= 2*target'. This (a) excludes unmanaged workers from cap, (b) accumulates crash history across cycles to prevent rapid churn bypass
4. In applyScaleDirective: reset d.unexpectedManagedExits = 0 on target change (fresh budget)
5. Remove totalWorkers variable (only used for old cap)

Test to write: TestReconcileScale_CapHoldsUnderRapidChurn
- target=3, simulate 3 cycles of spawn→connect→crash(via simulated heartbeat removal)→reconcileScale
- Assert total spawned <= 2*target=6 after all cycles

Existing test to update: TestReconcileScale_CapsAtDoubleTarget 'blocks spawn when total workers at 2x target'
- Currently uses 8 unmanaged workers to hit cap (which was the bug)
- After fix, unmanaged workers won't trigger cap; use unexpectedManagedExits instead

Files to change:
- pkg/dispatcher/worker_pool.go: checkHeartbeats - add managed field to deadInfo, increment counter
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go: add field, change cap logic in reconcileScale, reset in applyScaleDirective
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_autoscale_test.go: update existing test, add new churn test
close_reason: Cap now tracks managed exits only (unexpectedManagedExits). Unmanaged orphaned workers can no longer block managed spawning. Tests pass, gate clean. Commit: 8046cd3

title: Worker Claude process hangs on tail -f in TaskOutput
description:
During review, a worker's Claude process ran TaskOutput which spawned 'tail -f <output_file> | head -50'. The tail -f blocks indefinitely when the output file doesn't reach 50 lines, hanging the entire review phase.

Observed: PID 29661 running 'tail -f ...oro-rgux-18/tasks/b969d35.output' for ~2.6 hours on bead oro-rgux.18.

## Root Cause
TaskOutput uses 'tail -f' to follow a task output file. If the task completes with fewer lines than head expects, or if the task never writes enough output, tail -f blocks forever.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Identify how TaskOutput reads task output files and why tail -f hangs
- [ ] Add timeout or alternative read mechanism that doesn't block indefinitely
- [ ] Test: TaskOutput on a completed task with short output returns promptly

The `oro help` command (`cmd/oro/cmd_help.go`) displays a categorized overview of all subcommands. It is currently missing the `ingest` command, which IS registered in `root.go` but NOT listed in the help text.

Additionally, the project has no README.md or standalone CLI reference documentation — all docs are internal specs in `docs/plans/`.

## Current State

- `cmd/oro/cmd_help.go` lines 10-38: hardcoded `helpText` const with 6 categories (Lifecycle, Monitoring, Memory, Control, Search, Internal)
- `cmd/oro/root.go` lines 24-41: 15 registered commands
- Help text lists 14 commands — missing `ingest`
- Individual commands have good Cobra Short/Long help text
- `cmd/oro-dash/help.go` has context-sensitive help overlays (board, detail, insights, search views)
- No README.md at project root

## What Needs to Change

1. **Fix `oro help` text** (`cmd/oro/cmd_help.go`): Add `ingest` to the Memory category:
   ```
   Memory:
     remember   Store a memory
     recall     Search memories
     forget     Delete memories by ID
     memories   Browse and manage the memory store
     ingest     Import knowledge from JSONL file
   ```

2. **Verify all 15 registered commands appear in help text** — currently only `ingest` is missing, but the worker should confirm no others were added since.

3. **Add test** ensuring help text stays in sync with registered commands — a test that iterates root subcommands and asserts each appears in `helpText`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `oro help` output includes all commands registered in `root.go` (currently 15), including `ingest`
- [ ] A test in `cmd/oro/cmd_help_test.go` fails if a new command is registered but not added to the help text
- [ ] `go test ./cmd/oro/...` passes
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix DB split: CLI memories.db vs dispatcher state.db
description:
Discovery: `defaultMemoryStore()` in cmd/oro/store.go:13 opens `paths.MemoryDBPath` (~/.oro/memories.db), but the dispatcher and workers use `paths.StateDBPath` (~/.oro/state.db). Workers insert memories into state.db, but `oro memories list` reads from memories.db. This means CLI memory commands show stale/different data than what workers actually stored.

Investigate whether the split is intentional (worker isolation?) or a bug. If a bug, align both to the same DB. If intentional, document why and consider a sync mechanism.

title: Fix wrong branch in handleMergeConflictResult retry
description:
dispatcher.go:983 passes "main" as branch when retrying mergeAndComplete after ops conflict resolution. This causes isBranchMerged to check main..main (always 0), short-circuiting with main HEAD as the merge SHA. The bead gets closed with a phantom commit that may not contain the bead's actual code.

title: Add content verification to isBranchMerged guard
description:
merge.go:164-181 isBranchMerged checks rev-list --count main..<branch>. When count is 0, it returns true with main HEAD as the merge SHA. But count=0 can occur when branch=="main" (main..main) or when the branch was reset/force-pushed. The guard should also verify that the branch's content is actually on main.

Fix: After confirming count is 0, run `git diff main..<branch>`. If diff output is non-empty, the branch has content not on main — return false (not merged). If diff is empty, truly merged. On git diff error, return false (fail-open: proceed to rebase).

title: Fix ops merge prompt to guide agent through rebase resolution
description:
The current conflict resolution flow is broken: handleRebaseFailure (merge.go:185) runs git rebase --abort BEFORE the ops agent spawns. The ops agent is told to "Resolve conflicts in: <files>" but the worktree is clean — no conflict markers exist. The ops agent has nothing to resolve.

Fix: Update buildMergePrompt (ops.go:383-401) to instruct the ops agent to re-run the rebase itself. Add Branch field to MergeOpts (ops.go:103-109) so the prompt can reference the exact branch. Update the call site in dispatcher.go:859-862 to pass the branch.

New prompt should instruct:
1. git rebase main <branch> (re-trigger the conflict)
2. Resolve conflict markers in <files>
3. git add <resolved-files>
4. git rebase --continue
5. Run tests to verify

title: Dispatcher-spawned workers log to daemon log instead of per-worker files
description:
ExecProcessManager.Spawn (pkg/dispatcher/process_manager.go:88-89) sets cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout and cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr. When the dispatcher runs as a daemon, os.Stdout and os.Stderr are the daemon's log file (/tmp/oro-daemon.log), so all worker output (including claude -p stdout and stderr) gets mixed into the daemon log. Individual worker log files (~/.oro/workers/<id>/output.log) are never created for dispatcher-managed workers. This makes per-worker debugging impossible via oro logs or by inspecting worker log dirs.

Contrast with ExecWorkerSpawner.SpawnWorker (cmd/oro/cmd_worker_launch.go:28-52) which properly creates per-worker log files and redirects child stdout/stderr there.

Observed: ran oro start --detach with 3 workers. ls ~/.oro/workers/ | grep worker-177 showed only one worker-1771377396051711000-1 dir (the one launched via oro worker launch path), and its log was empty. Workers 0 and 2 had no log dirs at all because they were spawned by the dispatcher's reconcileScale -> ExecProcessManager.Spawn path.

Fix: Add oroHome string field to ExecProcessManager. In NewOroProcessManager, accept oroHome as parameter. In Spawn(id), create log dir at filepath.Join(oroHome, 'workers', id) via os.MkdirAll, open output.log (O_CREATE|O_WRONLY|O_APPEND), set cmd.Stdout = logFile and cmd.Stderr = logFile. Close parent copy of logFile after cmd.Start(). Thread oroHome through the call site in cmd/oro/cmd_start.go where NewOroProcessManager is called.

Read: pkg/dispatcher/process_manager.go:ExecProcessManager.Spawn (lines 86-110), cmd/oro/cmd_worker_launch.go:ExecWorkerSpawner.SpawnWorker (lines 28-52), cmd/oro/cmd_start.go (search for NewOroProcessManager call site)

Signature: func NewOroProcessManager(socketPath, oroHome string) *ExecProcessManager

Edges:
- oroHome empty string -> fall back to os.Stdout/os.Stderr with a logged warning (don't silently swallow output)
- log directory creation fails -> return error from Spawn (don't silently drop logs)
- log file open fails -> return error from Spawn
- parent closes its logFile fd after Start() -> child process still has the fd open (standard Go pattern, matches ExecWorkerSpawner)

Test: pkg/dispatcher/process_manager_test.go:TestOroProcessManagerWritesToWorkerLogFile | Cmd: go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... -run TestOroProcessManagerWritesToWorkerLogFile | Assert: NewOroProcessManager(sockPath, tmpDir) then Spawn('w-test'); verify file exists at tmpDir/workers/w-test/output.log; verify cmd.Stdout \!= os.Stdout (inject factory that exposes the built cmd for assertion)
close_reason: Implemented per-worker log files in ExecProcessManager.Spawn. NewOroProcessManager now accepts oroHome param, creates oroHome/workers/<id>/output.log for each worker, and redirects stdout/stderr there. Empty oroHome falls back to os.Stdout/Stderr with warning. Tests pass. Commit: 0fe32f2

title: Escalation retry loop replays stale WORKER_CRASH alerts with empty beadID

title: Dispatcher does not mark beads in_progress on assignment
description:
When the dispatcher assigns a bead to a worker, it does not call 'bd update <id> --status=in_progress'. This causes bd stats to report 0 in_progress while workers are actively executing beads. Some workers update status themselves but it's inconsistent — observed 3/7 assigned beads marked in_progress.

title: Update dispatching-parallel-agents skill: pipeline mode + oro workers
description:
Upgrade the dispatching-parallel-agents skill with these changes:

1. **Pipeline mode as default**: Merge-as-you-go instead of batch. Each completed worker is immediately merged and the next bead launched from the queue, keeping N workers saturated.

2. **Default to oro workers**: Use `oro work <bead-id>` as primary dispatch method (handles worktree, TDD, QG, ops review, merge). Raw Task agents become fallback.

3. **FF-merge with active worktrees**: Document that when workers are still running, you can't rebase (guard hook blocks). Use ff-merge when branch shares same base, cherry-pick when it diverges. No need to kill active workers.

4. **Dependency-aware scheduling**: Same file = sequential deps, different files = parallel. Document the pattern we used for dispatcher_test.go (7in4.4.1→.2→.3 sequential, 7in4.4.4-.7 parallel).

5. **Resource concurrency limits**: Default to 5 oro workers. Task agents can go higher (lighter weight). Document that resource contention (signal:killed) was observed at 2 concurrent claude processes in earlier sessions, but 5 is the target.

6. **Stale worktree preflight**: Check for orphaned worktrees from previous sessions at start. `git worktree list` and clean up.

7. **Error/retry strategy**: When a worker fails — inspect worktree state, fix and recommit manually, or re-dispatch. Don't blindly retry.

8. **bd file contention**: Multiple workers closing beads modify .beads/issues.jsonl. Note this as a known merge friction point — merge order doesn't matter for this file, just take latest.

Skill describes pipeline as default pattern. oro work is primary dispatch method. Raw Task agents documented as fallback. Merge-as-you-go replaces batch merge section.

title: Fix manager beacon startup sequence — skip 'oro start', go straight to directive
description:
## Problem
Manager beacon step 5 says: `Run oro start to launch the dispatcher (if not already running).`
But by the time the manager receives this beacon, `oro start` has ALREADY launched the dispatcher (it's what created the tmux session + injected the beacon). Running `oro start` again just prints "dispatcher already running (PID X)" and returns — the manager stalls.

## Root Cause
manager.go:35 — startup sequence assumes manager might need to start the dispatcher, but `oro start` always starts the dispatcher BEFORE creating the tmux session (cmd_start.go:64-84).

## Fix
Change the manager beacon startup sequence (manager.go lines 29-37) from:
```
5. Run `oro start` to launch the dispatcher (if not already running).
6. Run `oro directive scale N` to set the worker count to your chosen size.
```
To:
```
5. Run `oro directive status` to confirm the dispatcher is running.
6. Run `oro directive scale N` to set the worker count to your chosen size.
```

Also remove `oro start` from the Oro CLI section (line 43) or mark it as "used only by the human, not by the manager" since the manager never needs it.

## Files
- cmd/oro/manager.go (beacon text)
- cmd/oro/manager_test.go (update assertions if any reference the old text)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Manager beacon startup step 5 references `oro directive status` not `oro start`
- Manager beacon does not instruct manager to run `oro start`
- Manager test assertions updated to match new beacon text
- `go test ./cmd/oro/... -run TestManager` passes

title: Wire memory system end-to-end: inject into worker prompts, enable consolidation, hybrid search
description:
## Problem

The memory system (pkg/memory/) has substantial infrastructure built but much of it is NOT wired into production. Workers capture memories but never receive them back. Key gaps found by code audit:

### Not wired (marked //oro:testonly or never called)

1. **ForPrompt() never called** — `memory.ForPrompt()` builds a compact memory table for worker prompts, but nobody calls it in the prompt-building path (`worker.go:buildAssignPrompt`). Workers produce memories but never receive relevant ones. This is the biggest gap.

2. **Consolidate marked testonly** — `memory.Consolidate()` (prune stale + merge duplicates) is only callable via `oro memories consolidate` CLI. No automatic/periodic consolidation. Memory store grows unbounded.

3. **HybridSearch marked testonly** — RRF fusion of FTS5 + vector cosine similarity exists but production only uses plain FTS5 `Search()`. Degraded retrieval quality.

4. **SetEmbedder marked testonly** — TF-IDF embeddings are never computed in production inserts. Even if HybridSearch were enabled, there are no embeddings to search against.

### Partially wired (agent-dependent)

5. **LEARNED hook requires agent cooperation** — `memory_capture.py` hook only fires when agent explicitly runs `bd comment <id> "LEARNED: ..."`. Not truly automatic.

6. **Learning reminder hook is advisory only** — `learning_reminder.py` fires on git commit but only prints a reminder. Doesn't capture anything.

### What IS working

- Implicit extraction (`ExtractImplicit`) — scans worker stdout for "I learned...", "Gotcha:..." etc. Production-wired at worker.go:594.
- Marker extraction via `DrainOutput` — `[MEMORY]` markers parsed from stdout in real-time. Production-wired.
- Write-time dedup (Jaccard similarity). Working.
- Time decay scoring at query time. Working.
- `oro remember` / `oro recall` CLI commands. Working but manual.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ForPrompt()` called during `buildAssignPrompt()` — workers receive relevant memories in their prompt
- [ ] `//oro:testonly` removed from `Consolidate` — periodic or on-startup consolidation runs automatically
- [ ] `//oro:testonly` removed from `HybridSearch` — `ForPrompt` uses hybrid search when embedder available
- [ ] `//oro:testonly` removed from `SetEmbedder` — embedder initialized in production memory store setup
- [ ] Consolidation either runs on a schedule (e.g., on `oro start`) or has a wired trigger
- [ ] Integration test: worker receives a memory in its prompt that was created by a previous worker
- [ ] All existing tests still pass after wiring changes

## Test Command

```
go test ./pkg/memory/ ./pkg/worker/ ./cmd/oro/ -v -run TestMemor
```

## Files

- pkg/memory/memory.go (remove testonly, wire embedder)
- pkg/worker/worker.go (call ForPrompt in buildAssignPrompt)
- pkg/worker/prompt.go (may need memory injection point)
- cmd/oro/cmd_start.go (wire consolidation on startup)
- cmd/oro/cmd_memories.go (verify CLI still works)

title: Improve handoff mechanism to prevent empty context and missing AC in continuation beads
description:
Workers create continuation beads with empty 'Context from last handoff:' and no acceptance criteria, causing:
- New workers start from scratch with zero guidance
- MISSING_AC escalations from dispatcher
- Zombie beads proliferate (12+ cleaned this session)
- Handoff loops: oro-sh9f -> .1 -> .1.1 -> .1.2 (all empty context)

## Root Cause Analysis (verified against code)

Three locations create continuation beads, none pass acceptance criteria:

### 1. prompt.go:79-80 — Agent-initiated handoff
Template instructs agent to run: bd create --title="Continue: <bead-title>" --type=task --description="Remaining: <what's left>"
Missing: --acceptance-criteria flag, --parent flag, instructions to copy parent AC.

### 2. dispatcher.go:1048-1058 — handleHandoff() exhaustion path
Creates continuation via d.beads.Create() with only ContextSummary (often empty).
Never calls lookupBeadDetail() to get parent AC. No AC parameter in Create() signature.

### 3. beadsource.go:104-115 — CLIBeadSource.Create()
Function signature has no AC parameter at all. bd create command never gets --acceptance-criteria.

## Fix Design

### Fix 1: Add AC parameter to CLIBeadSource.Create() (beadsource.go)
Add `acceptanceCriteria string` parameter. When non-empty, append `--acceptance-criteria=<ac>` to bd create args.
Update BeadSource interface in dispatcher.go:60 to match.

### Fix 2: Pass parent AC in handleHandoff() (dispatcher.go:1048-1058)
Before creating continuation, call lookupBeadDetail(ctx, beadID, workerID) to get parent title + AC.
Pass AC to d.beads.Create(). Include parent title in continuation description for context.

### Fix 3: Update prompt template (prompt.go:79-80)
Change agent handoff instructions to include --parent and --acceptance-criteria flags.
Template should be: bd create --title="Continue: <bead-title>" --type=task --parent=<bead-id> --description="Remaining: <what's left>" --acceptance-criteria="<copy parent AC>"

## Evidence
oro-sh9f, oro-5srh.1, oro-ycjj.1.1, oro-ldbd.1, oro-mcxf.1, oro-5srh.3.1 all had empty handoff contexts.
lookupBeadDetail() already exists at dispatcher.go:1753 and is used in review path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Continuation beads created by handoff include parent AC
- Continuation beads include bead title from parent
- Worker context is never empty when picking up a continuation bead

title: Skip mutation testing in pre-push hook (keep tiers 1-3)

## Problem

title: Add oro help command with categorized subcommand overview
description:
## Problem

Oro uses default Cobra help (\`oro -h\`), which lists all 14 subcommands in a flat, alphabetical list with no grouping. For a CLI with distinct operational categories (lifecycle, memory, debugging, internal), a custom help command would improve discoverability.

## Current State

14 subcommands registered in cmd/oro/root.go:
- Lifecycle: init, start, stop, cleanup
- Monitoring: status, logs, dash
- Memory: remember, recall, forget, memories (list, consolidate)
- Control: directive
- Search: index (build, search)
- Internal: worker (not user-facing)

Default \`oro --help\` shows them all flat. No \`oro help\` subcommand exists.

## Design

Add a custom \`oro help\` command that displays subcommands grouped by category with brief descriptions:

\`\`\`
Oro — Agent swarm orchestrator

Lifecycle:
  init       Bootstrap dependencies and generate config
  start      Launch the swarm (tmux + dispatcher + workers)
  stop       Graceful shutdown
  cleanup    Clean all stale state after a crash

Monitoring:
  status     Show current swarm state
  logs       Query and tail dispatcher event logs
  dash       Launch interactive dashboard

Memory:
  remember   Store a memory
  recall     Search memories
  forget     Delete memories by ID
  memories   Browse and manage the memory store

Control:
  directive  Send a directive to the dispatcher (scale, focus, pause, resume)

Search:
  index      Semantic code search (build, search)

Use "oro <command> --help" for detailed usage of any command.
\`\`\`

### Implementation
- Add cmd/oro/cmd_help.go with a \`newHelpCmd()\` function
- Override the root command's default help template OR add \`help\` as a subcommand
- Group commands by category using cobra command groups or manual formatting

## Files to Modify
- cmd/oro/cmd_help.go — New file: custom help command
- cmd/oro/cmd_help_test.go — New file: test help output
- cmd/oro/root.go — Register help command

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test: cmd/oro/cmd_help_test.go:TestHelpOutput | Cmd: go test -race ./cmd/oro/... -run TestHelpOutput | Assert: Help output contains category headers (Lifecycle, Monitoring, Memory, Control, Search) and all 14 subcommands
- [ ] \`oro help\` displays categorized command list
- [ ] \`oro help <command>\` falls through to cobra's default per-command help

Read: cmd/oro/root.go:newRootCmd, cmd/oro/cmd_status.go (example subcommand pattern)

title: Add one-shot claude -p manager as first responder for dispatcher escalations
description:
Add a one-shot manager tier between the dispatcher and the persistent interactive manager. When the dispatcher detects an escalation (STUCK_WORKER, MERGE_CONFLICT, PRIORITY_CONTENTION, MISSING_AC), it spawns a short-lived 'claude -p' process with a manager playbook + escalation context + recent history from the persistent escalation queue. The one-shot handles routine cases autonomously; unresolved escalations bubble up to the persistent manager.

## Open Design Question
How does the dispatcher know if the one-shot succeeded?
- Option A: Ack-based — one-shot must ack the escalation via CLI before exiting. Unacked = failed.
- Option B: State verification — dispatcher re-checks the triggering condition after process exit. Problem persists = failed.
- Option C: Both — ack proves agent tried, state check proves it worked.
Worker should evaluate and pick.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dispatcher spawns claude -p with manager playbook on escalation
- [ ] One-shot receives escalation type, bead context, and recent escalation history as prompt
- [ ] One-shot has access to oro directive and bd CLI commands
- [ ] Dispatcher detects one-shot failure and escalates to persistent manager
- [ ] One-shot timeout prevents runaway processes (e.g., 5 min max)
- [ ] Escalations that the one-shot resolves are marked acked in the persistent queue

title: Rework role identity: env vars + SessionStart hook instead of send-keys beacon
description:
Adopt the Gastown pattern for role identity. Currently oro puts all role differentiation weight on a fragile tmux send-keys beacon injection that silently fails for large payloads.

Gastown pattern to adopt:
1. Unique tmux session names per role (e.g. oro-architect, oro-manager instead of oro:0.0/oro:0.1)
2. Environment variables set at launch: ORO_ROLE=architect/manager, BD_ACTOR=architect/manager, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=architect/manager
3. SessionStart hook reads ORO_ROLE and injects role-specific context (architect beacon vs manager beacon) — no need for send-keys of huge strings
4. Separate working directories per role (or at minimum separate session storage)
5. Beacon becomes a small nudge/kick, not the entire role prompt

This replaces the current approach in cmd/oro/tmux.go where Create() sends the full ArchitectBeacon()/ManagerBeacon() (~100-150 lines each) via tmux send-keys.

Files to change:
- cmd/oro/tmux.go — session creation, pane naming, env var injection
- .claude/hooks/ — add ORO_ROLE-aware SessionStart hook that injects role context
- cmd/oro/architect.go — beacon becomes hook-injectable context, not send-keys payload
- cmd/oro/manager.go — same
- cmd/oro/cmd_start.go — wire new session names

Reference: Gastown internal/config/env.go (AgentEnv), internal/session/names.go, SessionStart hook pattern.
close_reason: Role identity reworked with env vars + hooks. Tests pass.

title: Add per-type pre-check guard to escalation retry loop
description:
retryPendingEscalations (dispatcher.go:2448) blindly re-fires all pending escalations every 2 minutes without checking if the underlying condition still holds. It SELECTs only id, message — doesnt read the type or bead_id columns that are already stored in the escalations table. This causes infinite escalation spam for conditions already resolved (MISSING_AC after AC is added, STUCK_WORKER after worker is gone, MERGE_CONFLICT after branch merged).

This supersedes oro-etbo (MISSING_AC-only fix) by implementing the guard for ALL escalation types.

Fix: (1) Change SELECT to include type, bead_id. (2) Add shouldRetryEscalation(ctx, escType, beadID) method with per-type guards. (3) If condition resolved, auto-ack the escalation row (UPDATE escalations SET status=acked WHERE id=?) instead of re-sending.

Per-type guards:
- MISSING_AC: beads.Show -> AC populated -> auto-ack
- STUCK_WORKER: worker not in d.workers -> auto-ack
- WORKER_CRASH: bead not in_progress (re-queued or closed) -> auto-ack
- STUCK: bead status changed from in_progress -> auto-ack
- MERGE_CONFLICT: bead closed -> auto-ack
- PRIORITY_CONTENTION: bead is in_progress (picked up) -> auto-ack
acceptance_criteria:
Test: pkg/dispatcher/escalation_precheck_test.go:TestShouldRetryEscalation | Cmd: go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... -run TestShouldRetryEscalation | Assert: For each escalation type, shouldRetryEscalation returns false when the underlying condition is resolved. retryPendingEscalations auto-acks resolved rows instead of re-sending.
Read: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:retryPendingEscalations (lines 2448-2469), pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:escalate (lines 2364-2385), pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:parseEscalationType (lines 2474-2488), pkg/protocol/types.go:EscalationType constants (lines 86-96)
Signature: func (d *Dispatcher) shouldRetryEscalation(ctx context.Context, escType string, beadID string) bool
Edges: beadID is empty -> return true (always retry if no bead context); beads.Show returns error -> return true (retry on error, dont suppress); unknown escType -> return true (dont block future types)

title: Implement: ops agent spawner (short-lived claude -p for review, merge conflict, diagnosis)

title: Add persistent escalation queue with retry for dispatcher-to-manager messages
description:
The dispatcher sends escalations to the manager via tmux paste-buffer + send-keys (fire-and-forget). If the manager is interrupted (user input, context compaction, session clear), the message is lost. The dispatcher has no way to detect this and never retries.

The dispatcher already has a persistent store (state.db with an events table) and already uses file-based signals for the pane monitor (handoff_requested/handoff_complete). Escalations should be similarly durable.

Design options (worker should evaluate and pick):

Option A — Persistent queue in SQLite:
- Write escalations to a new escalations table (id, type, bead_id, message, created_at, acked_at)
- Dispatcher retries unacked escalations every N minutes via tmux
- Manager runs oro directive ack-escalation <id> after processing

Option B — File-based queue (simpler):
- Write escalations to ~/.oro/panes/manager/escalations/ as individual files
- Manager's SessionStart hook reads and displays pending escalations
- Manager deletes file after processing

Option C — Hybrid:
- Store in SQLite for durability and queryability
- Use file signal to wake the manager (like handoff_requested pattern)
- Manager reads pending escalations via oro directive pending-escalations

Key constraint: tmux paste-buffer is unreliable as a delivery mechanism. The solution must not depend on tmux delivery succeeding on the first attempt.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Escalations survive manager interruption/restart/compaction
- [ ] Unacknowledged escalations are retried (with backoff or periodic check)
- [ ] Manager can list and ack pending escalations via CLI
- [ ] No duplicate processing (idempotent ack)
- [ ] Existing escalation types (MERGE_CONFLICT, STUCK_WORKER, PRIORITY_CONTENTION, WORKER_CRASH) are routed through the new queue
notes: Implementation EXISTS in commit b4a8811 (merged to main). Escalations table schema, pending-escalations/ack-escalation directives, and retry loop are all implemented. False alarm on 'no code committed'. BLOCKED: Requires daemon startup to create escalations table via schema migration. Daemon has never been started on this system.
close_reason: Persistent escalation queue implemented. Escalations table in SQLite, pending-escalations and ack-escalation directives, retry loop every 2 min (max 5). Commit b4a8811. All tests pass.

title: Fix idle worker reconnect sends empty BeadID causing spurious rejections
description:
When an idle worker reconnects after a network glitch, it sends MsgReconnect with BeadID='' (empty string). The dispatcher's validateReconnectBead() tries to look up bead '' which always fails, logging reconnect_closed_bead_rejected. The worker should re-register as idle cleanly without going through bead validation.

Root cause: pkg/worker/worker.go reconnect logic always sends a Reconnect message with whatever beadID is set (empty for idle workers).

Fix: In the dispatcher's reconnect handler (dispatcher.go), if BeadID is empty, skip bead validation and transition worker directly to idle state.
close_reason: Guard validateReconnectBead behind non-empty BeadID check

title: Simplify restart-oro skill: replace manual Phase 2 cleanup with oro cleanup
description:
## Problem

The restart-oro skill (.claude/commands/restart-oro.md) has redundant cleanup steps. Phase 1 already calls \`./oro cleanup\` which handles tmux kill, dispatcher kill, worker kill, worktree prune, agent branch deletion, and bead reset. Phase 2 then manually repeats most of these same operations.

## Current State

**Phase 1** (Kill Everything):
- \`tmux kill-session -t oro\` — redundant, oro cleanup does this
- \`./oro cleanup\` — the comprehensive cleanup command
- \`pkill -f "oro start/worker"\` — belt-and-suspenders

**Phase 2** (Clean Stale State):
- \`git worktree prune\` — already done by oro cleanup (cleanupWorktrees)
- \`git branch -D agent/*\` — already done by oro cleanup (cleanupAgentBranches)
- \`rm -rf .worktrees/\` — NOT done by oro cleanup (it only prunes references)
- Verification commands — still useful

**oro cleanup implementation** (cmd/oro/cmd_cleanup.go):
1. cleanupTmux — kills tmux session
2. cleanupDispatcher — signals dispatcher via SIGINT
3. cleanupWorkers — kills worker processes
4. cleanupPIDFile — removes stale PID file
5. cleanupSocketFile — removes stale socket file
6. cleanupWorktrees — runs git worktree prune
7. cleanupAgentBranches — deletes agent/* branches
8. cleanupBeads — resets in_progress beads to open

## Changes

### 1. Add .worktrees/ directory removal to oro cleanup

Add a new step in runCleanup (cmd/oro/cmd_cleanup.go) between cleanupWorktrees and cleanupAgentBranches:

```go
// cleanupWorktreeDir force-removes the .worktrees/ directory.
func cleanupWorktreeDir(cfg *cleanupConfig) bool {
    dir := filepath.Join(".", ".worktrees")
    if _, err := os.Stat(dir); errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
        return false
    }
    fmt.Fprintf(cfg.w, "removing .worktrees/ directory\n")
    if err := os.RemoveAll(dir); err != nil {
        fmt.Fprintf(cfg.w, "warning: remove .worktrees/: %v\n", err)
    }
    return true
}
```

### 2. Simplify restart-oro skill Phase 2

Replace the manual git commands in Phase 2 with just verification:

```markdown
## Phase 2: Verify Clean State

\`\`\`bash
git worktree list
git branch | grep agent/ || echo "No stale agent branches"
ls .worktrees/ 2>/dev/null || echo "No worktree directory"
\`\`\`

All cleanup is handled by \`oro cleanup\` in Phase 1. This phase only verifies.
```

## Files to Modify
- cmd/oro/cmd_cleanup.go — Add cleanupWorktreeDir step
- cmd/oro/cmd_cleanup_test.go — Test the new cleanup step
- .claude/commands/restart-oro.md — Simplify Phase 2 to verification only

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test: cmd/oro/cmd_cleanup_test.go:TestCleanupWorktreeDir | Cmd: go test -race ./cmd/oro/... -run TestCleanupWorktreeDir | Assert: .worktrees/ directory is removed when it exists; no error when it doesn't exist
- [ ] restart-oro.md Phase 2 no longer contains manual git worktree prune or git branch -D commands
- [ ] oro cleanup removes .worktrees/ directory when present

Read: cmd/oro/cmd_cleanup.go:runCleanup,cleanupWorktrees, cmd/oro/cmd_cleanup_test.go, .claude/commands/restart-oro.md
close_reason: Tests pass, gate clean. Commit: 901097b

title: Add dev-sync Makefile target and .envrc for automatic asset sync
description:
Add a dev-sync target to the Makefile that copies assets/ to ~/.oro/ with explicit path mapping (not a flat copy). Add .envrc that triggers dev-sync on directory entry.

Path mapping (assets/ is NOT 1:1 with ~/.oro/):
  assets/hooks/     -> ~/.oro/hooks/
  assets/skills/    -> ~/.oro/.claude/skills/
  assets/beacons/   -> ~/.oro/beacons/
  assets/commands/  -> ~/.oro/.claude/commands/
  assets/CLAUDE.md  -> ~/.oro/.claude/CLAUDE.md

.envrc must guard against worktree collision — only sync from main branch:
  source .venv/bin/activate 2>/dev/null
  if [ "$(git branch --show-current)" = "main" ] && [ -d assets ]; then
    make dev-sync 2>&1 | tail -1
  fi

dev-sync must:
  - Print what it copied (not silent)
  - Fail loudly on errors (no 2>/dev/null swallowing)
  - End with sanity check (verify at least one file at each target path)
  - Create target dirs if missing

Acceptance:
Test: Cmd: echo '# marker' >> assets/hooks/enforce-skills.sh && make dev-sync && grep marker ~/.oro/hooks/enforce-skills.sh
Assert: Change in assets/ appears in ~/.oro/ after dev-sync. Sanity check prints ok for all 5 target paths.

title: Allow architect to commit markdown and sync beads
description:
The architect_router.py PreToolUse hook currently blocks all Bash commands from the architect pane. This prevents the architect from committing its own output (specs in docs/plans/, decisions in ~/.oro/projects/, handoff YAML). The human has to manually commit architect work, which breaks flow.

Relax the hook to allow:
- git add *.md *.yaml *.yml (markdown and YAML only)
- git commit (when only markdown/YAML files are staged)
- git status, git diff, git log (read-only git commands)
- bd sync, bd create, bd update, bd close, bd list, bd show, bd ready, bd stats (all beads commands)
- git push (after committing markdown/beads only)

Continue blocking:
- git add on .go, .py, .sh, .js, .ts or any code files
- git commit when code files are staged
- make, go build, go test, go install
- Any command that modifies code

Implementation: in architect_router.py, add an allowlist check before the block/route decision. Parse the command to detect git add/commit/push with only markdown/YAML targets. Use git diff --cached --name-only to verify staged files are markdown-only before allowing commit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Architect can run: git add docs/plans/foo.md && git commit -m 'docs: add spec'
- [ ] Architect can run: bd sync && git push
- [ ] Architect CANNOT run: git add cmd/oro/foo.go
- [ ] Architect CANNOT run: git commit when .go/.py/.sh files are staged
- [ ] Architect CAN run: git status, git log, git diff (read-only)
close_reason: Implemented architect markdown/yaml git workflow. Updated architect_router.py hook to allow git add/commit/push for markdown and yaml files while blocking code files. All acceptance criteria verified with comprehensive tests.
